messages.author: 65fb1c2991af5c07
messages.subject: basis for spde
parts:
Hi there,

 

I am now modeling the spde on sphere, and trying to use spherical harmonic as basis on kappa and tau by

basis.T <-inla.mesh.basis(mesh, type="sph.harm", n=3)

basis.K <-inla.mesh.basis(mesh, type="sph.harm", n=3)

spde <-inla.spde.create(mesh, model="matern", param=list(basis.K, basis.T))

 

data$spatial <- mesh$idx$loc

formula = y ~ -1 + f(spatial, model=spde)

result = inla( formula, data, family="gaussian", verbose=TRUE)

But the result is exactly the same with the case “spde <-inla.spde.create(mesh, model="matern")”. The basis formulation seems not working. Does there has any further detail I should concern?

 

The second question is that I use the function “inla.spde2.matern”, I see the manual writing that B.tau and B.kappa are the matrix with specification of log-linear model. What the exact mean and requirement for formulating the matrix?

 

Thanks in advance

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: basis for spde
parts:
The problem here is the R syntax; inla.spde.create requires the parameters in the param list to be named, so you need
  param=list(basis.K=basis.K, basis.T=basis.T)

But be careful with your choice of basis; Spherical harmonics with order=3 gives 9 basis functions, which in turn will give you 18 hyperparameters (9 each for kappa^2 and tau) for inla to estimate, which is quite a lot!

> The second question is that I use the function “inla.spde2.matern”, I see the manual writing that B.tau and B.kappa are the matrix with specification of log-linear model. What the exact mean and requirement for formulating the matrix?

A brief mathematical definition is provided in the help text for inla.spde2.matern (more documentation is on its way...); to obtain the same model as for inla.spde.create, you can set
  B.tau=cbind(0, basis.T, basis.K*0)
  B.kappa=cbind(0, basis.T*0, basis.K/2)
The first column is an offset, and the rest are weigthed together from a common parameter vector theta.  The "/2" is there because inla.spde2.matern works with "log(kappa)", whereas inla.spde.create works with "log(kappa^2)".

/Finn

In the paper, the operator L_2= (b(s) + B(s)^t *{laplace}), does the b(s) means the basis.T ?
If I like to add B matrix to the model, can I further take others basis, says basis.B1 and basis.B2.
Then add Laplace operator to (basis.B1 + basis.B2)...use the result plus the basis.T will be the operator L_2, right?

Kylan

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: basis for spde
parts:
Hi,

the non-stationary models in Bolin and Lindgren (2011) are not implemented in r-inla, only the non-stationary models from Lindgren et al (2011).
The code in the package _can_ be used to construct the necessary matrices for the Bolin&Lindgren models, but that is not yet documented, and you would need to write your own code for doing estimation, since those models fall outside the r-inla model framework due to the complicated structure in the observation equation.  This may be changed in a future r-inla version, but a general implementation of all the Bolin&Lindgren models would be a lot of work.

/Finn
